## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-anonymized: neither authors nor reviewers know each other's identity, per the journal's review-process page (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/economics-and-philosophy/information/peer-review-information/review-process). Authors' identity is known to all Editors. The publisher's ethics page adds that the journal usually requires at least two independent reviewers (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/economics-and-philosophy/information/journal-policies/publishing-ethics). Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No transfer or cascade policy appears on the review-process, submitting, ethics or instructions pages read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | No publication of reports is mentioned on the pages read. Reports are forwarded to the author in full, and the Editors do not endorse a report's tone, per the contributor PDF (https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-file-manager/file/575a92f146b470010ae19e2d), retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | SciRev reports 1.0 average review rounds, n = 3 (https://scirev.org/journal/economics-and-philosophy/). The contributor PDF gives a revision deadline of eight months for a first revision and shorter ones later; a paper not resubmitted by then counts as withdrawn. Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Editorial decision rests with the Editors and may differ from the referees' advice. A Lead Editor (rotating among 4 Editors in the PDF text, though the live board page lists 3) screens each paper and either assigns it or rejects it without external review, giving a reason; the decision letter and reports are circulated to the other Editors before the author is told (contributor PDF above, retrieved 2026-11-23) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | A section "Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Tools" sits on the journal's own preparing-your-materials page and refers to the publisher's research publishing ethics guidelines; whether the wording is identical across the publisher's journals was not checked. Source: https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/economics-and-philosophy/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials, retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No permission gate found; use is allowed with declaration |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with mandatory declaration for generative uses; same rubric as the Mind and Educational Philosophy and Theory entries) |
| **Summary** | AI tools cannot be listed as authors. Authors must declare and describe use of an AI tool to generate text or images (translation included) or to analyse data; minimal non-generative uses such as spelling or language checking need no declaration. The declaration goes in an acknowledgments section or footnote, in the methods section for data work, or in figure captions for images, and names the tool and version, dates of use and how it was used. Accountability stays with the author. Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Source URL** | https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/economics-and-philosophy/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials |

## Format

> Sources: the contributor-instructions PDF (https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-file-manager/file/575a92f146b470010ae19e2d, text dated "Last updated January 5, 2023"), the preparing-your-materials page, the final-version PDF for accepted articles (https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-file-manager/file/59478a6fd664c46a06fb063b, undated) and the author-instructions page. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Article, Book Review, Critical Notice, Discussion Article, Reply, Symposium Article, Symposium Introduction; the page marks Article, Critical Notice, Discussion Article, Symposium Article and Symposium Introduction as research articles for open-access funding (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/economics-and-philosophy/information/author-instructions). Unsolicited book reviews are not considered. Short comments on or replies to published papers are considered |
| **Word limit** | The Editors prefer papers of fewer than 12,000 words and may return longer papers without review with a request to shorten (contributor PDF). A reply to a comment may be answered by the original author with up to 300 words |
| **Word limit negotiability** | A stated preference, not a hard cap, but the same sentence says longer papers may be returned unreviewed. Whether references, notes or appendices count toward 12,000 is not stated |
| **Abstract limit** | Not stated for the submission stage in the contributor PDF. The final-version instructions for accepted articles require an abstract not exceeding 100 words and up to five keywords |
| **Reference limit** | No cap stated. Citations are author-date with page numbers after a colon, for example Author (2014: 47); footnotes only sparingly and never just to carry a citation; endnotes are acceptable for review but the final version uses footnotes |
| **Supplementary material** | Allowed as online supplementary materials (appendices, tables, datasets, video, sound), published alongside the article and not typeset (preparing-your-materials page) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Final version: each figure or table in a separate file, TIF or EPS preferred, raster at 300 dpi or more, captions required, accessibility descriptions required by the publisher (final-version PDF and preparing-your-materials page) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** One scope condition, stated by the journal: it publishes only articles that engage with issues of interest to both economists and philosophers (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/economics-and-philosophy/information/author-instructions; also in the contributor PDF, https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-file-manager/file/575a92f146b470010ae19e2d). Retrieved 2026-11-23.
- **What kind of engagement?** Topics named in the aims: foundations of rational or behavioral decision theory and game theory, the nature of rationality, economics intersecting moral, political and social philosophy, experimental research on economics and philosophy, and the philosophy and methodology of economics (same page). Articles that use mathematics must be written to be accessible to readers with limited formal training (same page).
- **History and exegesis**: the journal says it does not publish historical or text-interpretive work unless it contributes to current debates about economics and philosophy (same page). Regex `\b(Aristotle|Aquinas|Hobbes|Locke|Hume|Smith|Marx|Mill|Bentham|Sidgwick)\b` (case-sensitive) matches 4 of 167 abstract-bearing records of 2021-2026 (2.4%), so the explicit scope limit is consistent with what is published.
- **Previous work**: if a paper is closely related to the author's earlier work, it must discuss how (contributor PDF, same URL as above).
- **Article types**: Article, Book Review, Critical Notice, Discussion Article, Reply, Symposium Article, Symposium Introduction; book reviews are not accepted unsolicited (stated on the journal's book-reviews page, https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/economics-and-philosophy/information/about-this-journal/book-reviews, and repeated in the article-type list of the author-instructions page, https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/economics-and-philosophy/information/author-instructions; both read 2026-11-23).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Authors of papers rejected without external review are given a reason (contributor PDF). Whether out-of-scope work is a common ground for that rejection is not stated; the journal's 2017 report counts 125 of 227 decisions as rejections without external review (55%), without giving reasons (https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-file-manager/file/575a935f8d9f13e91d15f5c7).

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are Crossref journal-article records of 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23 whose title or abstract matches the stated regex (case-insensitive, flags `re.IGNORECASE`, word-boundary anchored); the denominator is the 167 records that carry an abstract. The thresholds are this research pass's own convention, not an external standard: share 0 = score 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; scores 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. Scores measure how often a method appears in the record set, not how a reviewer would treat it. The schema's rows were kept; two rows were added because the schema's rows do not describe an economics-and-philosophy venue (marked "added row"), and the autoethnography row does not fit this venue (it is kept for schema compatibility, with its count). ### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored (no editorial rule on first person found). In 167 abstract-bearing records of 2021-2026: regex `\b(I\|my\|me)\b` (case-sensitive) 87 (52.1%); regex `\bI (argue\|claim\|show\|defend\|propose\|suggest\|contend\|develop\|offer\|maintain\|explore)\b` (case-sensitive) 59 (35.3%); regex `\b(we\|our)\b` (case-insensitive) 65 (38.9%). Examples among the newest records: "I argue" in https://doi.org/10.1017/s0266267126100777, "Prices, I argue" in https://doi.org/10.1017/s0266267126100844, "We consider axioms" in https://doi.org/10.1017/s0266267126100807 (retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Expected density** | Editors prefer fewer than 12,000 words (contributor PDF, https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-file-manager/file/575a92f146b470010ae19e2d). The publisher's metrics page counts 31 articles for 2024 (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/economics-and-philosophy/information/about-this-journal/journal-metrics). The instructions ask for writing that is "attractive, and as clear and easy to follow as possible" (same PDF) |
| **Abstract and keywords** | For the final version of an accepted article: abstract of at most 100 words and up to five keywords, running title of at most 60 characters (final-version PDF, https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-file-manager/file/59478a6fd664c46a06fb063b). The submission-stage abstract rule is not stated in the PDF read |
| **Writing style notes** | Author-date citations with a colon before page numbers, "Author (2014: 47)"; no "ibid."; footnotes used sparingly and not for citations alone; headings numbered with numerals only, even for "Introduction"; consistent UK or US spelling; theorem-like environments (theorems, propositions, lemmas, examples, definitions) have set typography; mathematics typed in italics where italic (final-version PDF above and https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/economics-and-philosophy/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials) |
| **Authorship pattern** | Crossref author lists exist for 202 of the 227 records of 2021-2026 (https://api.crossref.org/works?filter=issn:0266-2671,from-pub-date:2021-01-01,until-pub-date:2026-11-23): 152 single-author (75.2%), 39 two authors, 9 three, 2 four or more. Book reviews and other non-article items are inside the 227 |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | Blank. No ethics-approval or human-subjects statement appears on the publishing-ethics page (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/economics-and-philosophy/information/journal-policies/publishing-ethics), the preparing-your-materials page or the contributor PDF, all read 2026-11-23; the output is mostly non-empirical by the counts above, which is not an ethics rule |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author work is the norm: 152 of 202 Crossref records with author lists, 2021-2026 (75.2%) (https://api.crossref.org/works?filter=issn:0266-2671,from-pub-date:2021-01-01,until-pub-date:2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | The affiliation rule asks for the institution where the research was conducted, supported or approved; no independent-scholar rule is stated (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/economics-and-philosophy/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials). In double-anonymous review the author's affiliation is not seen by reviewers (review-process page). Decisions are made without reference to funding, and corresponding authors without an agreement, an equity-initiative or grant coverage can ask for an APC discount or waiver after acceptance (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/economics-and-philosophy/information/journal-policies/open-access-options). Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Encouraged, not required: the research-transparency page encourages Data Availability Statements and deposit in a repository that provides persistent identifiers (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/economics-and-philosophy/information/journal-policies/research-transparency), retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-anonymized review; the paper must be anonymized so a referee cannot infer the author, with self-citation rewritten in the third person; acknowledgments and the competing-interests declaration are left out of the anonymized file and given in a cover letter; a non-anonymized version can be submitted with an explanation of why anonymizing is impossible (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/economics-and-philosophy/information/author-instructions/submitting-your-materials and contributor PDF). A preprint may be posted at any time (open-access-options page). ORCID is required for corresponding authors (submitting page). Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **AI use** | Declaration needed for generative or analytic uses; AI cannot be an author (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/economics-and-philosophy/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials), retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Open access and cost** | Gold open access for research articles; APC GBP 2,610 or USD 3,655 where no agreement or waiver applies (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/economics-and-philosophy/information/author-instructions/fees-and-pricing), retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Prior publication and concurrent submission** | A manuscript must not be under consideration, accepted or in press elsewhere without agreement of all parties; preprints are not prior publication (preparing-your-materials page) |

**Method notes:** OpenAlex was used for window totals, group-bys and the top-cited list (about 12 group-by requests plus the scaffold script's own calls, spaced 2 s, no key and no contact address, no HTTP 429 seen; the dry-run and scaffold calls were made before these); a first group-by attempt returned truncated groups because page size was 1, and was rerun with a larger page size. Keyword counts use Crossref text, because the regexes need a record set to run over; they were run in Python with `re` and flags stated per cell, over journal-article records only. The all-lowercase first-person check was dropped because a case-insensitive "I" also matches enumerators such as "(i)"; the case-sensitive version is reported. The method-row scores use the pass's own thresholds stated under Methodological Preferences.

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope**: the journal publishes only articles of interest to both economists and philosophers, and says authors should check scope before submitting (Framing Requirements; https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/economics-and-philosophy/information/author-instructions/submitting-your-materials). A paper that speaks to only one of the two audiences is outside the stated scope.
- **Length**: the Editors prefer papers under 12,000 words and may return longer ones without review (Format; contributor PDF). The pages do not say whether references count.
- **Anonymisation**: submissions must be anonymized, and a paper that can be anonymized but is not will be returned (Peer Review, Practical Concerns; submitting page). A non-anonymized version is considered only with a reason the Editors accept.
- **Prior or concurrent publication**: a paper under consideration, accepted or in press elsewhere is not allowed without agreement of all parties; preprints are not counted as prior publication (Practical Concerns; preparing-your-materials page).
- **History and exegesis**: purely historical or text-interpretive work is outside scope unless it contributes to current debates (Framing Requirements; aims text).
- **AI use**: undeclared generative use breaches the declaration rule (AI Policy).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact read; ethics-approval rules are unknown (Practical Concerns blank).

### Soft Tax

- **Desk screening**: the journal's own reports show 53.9% of 2014 decisions and 55% of 2017 decisions were rejections without external review (Metrics: Desk Rejection Rate); the figures are old and no newer one was found. The 2014 median time for these decisions was 14 days, and SciRev's immediate-rejection figure is also 14 days (Review Cycle Time).
- **Time when reviewed**: the 2014 median was 66 days to a decision after external review, and SciRev gives 2.0 months for the first round (n = 3) (Review Cycle Time); a first revision may have up to eight months (Peer Review).
- **Cost**: where no agreement or funding applies, the APC for a research article is GBP 2,610 or USD 3,655, with discount or waiver requests handled by the publisher after acceptance and not by the Editors (Open Access).
- **Mathematical accessibility**: mathematical content must be readable by people with limited formal training (Framing Requirements); how strictly this is applied is not stated.
- **Anonymising effort**: self-citations rewritten, acknowledgments and competing-interest declaration moved to a cover letter (Practical Concerns).

### Best Suited For

- Normative economics and moral or political philosophy that cites welfare, justice or distributive principles: 62 of 167 abstract-bearing records match the welfare-and-justice regex, and the three largest OpenAlex primary topics are Political Philosophy and Ethics (67), Philosophical Ethics and Theory (29) and Decision-Making and Behavioral Economics (22) (Epistemological, Top Topics).
- Decision-theoretic and game-theoretic work, formal or axiomatic: 12 and 11 of 167 for the two regexes, 15 for theorem and axiom terms (Epistemological, Methodological Preferences).
- Single-authored arguments in the first person: 152 of 202 author lists are single-author, and "I argue"-type phrasing is in 59 of 167 abstract-bearing records (Voice & Style).
- Authors outside funded institutions needing an open-access route: the publisher states waivers and discounts are decided separately from acceptance (Open Access, Practical Concerns).

### Not Recommended For

- Primarily econometric or observational empirical work: econometric regex 0 of 167, "empirical" 7 (Methodological Preferences). The counts show it is rare here, not that it is rejected.
- Qualitative, mixed-methods or review-style submissions: all three regexes 0 of 167 (Methodological Preferences).
- Historical or exegetical studies with no bearing on current debates (aims text; Framing Requirements).
- Topics on AI, religion, race and colonialism: regexes 0 of 167 each (Sensitive Topics); this shows absence from the abstracts of the sample, not editorial refusal.
- Anyone needing a current turnaround figure: the journal's own decision times are for 2014 and SciRev has 3 reviews (Review Cycle Time).

### Rejection Fallback Chain

> No source states where rejected authors usually go. The rows below are topical neighbours that already exist in this corpus, listed only because they share subject area (philosophy and economics, or normative philosophy); they are not a claim about acceptance odds.

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Erasmus Journal for Philosophy and Economics](../philosophy/erasmus-journal-for-philosophy-and-economics-ejpe.md) | Same two-discipline subject area; an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
| 2 | [Utilitas](../philosophy/utilitas.md) | Welfare and utilitarian terms are the largest keyword group here (62 of 167); an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
| 3 | [Philosophy and Public Affairs](../philosophy/philosophy-and-public-affairs.md) | Moral and political philosophy neighbour; an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
